judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same grain, same resolved rank 1) within Strand 4: Data, but in different sub-strands: B5.4.2.1.3 sits under Chance (Probability) and asks learners to conduct a probability experiment repeatedly, record outcomes and explain results; B5.4.1.1.1 sits under Data Collection, Organisation, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis and asks learners to explain the difference between first-hand and second-hand data. The coherence is substantive rather than merely lexical: recording the outcomes of an experiment one conducts is a concrete instance of generating first-hand data, so the probability experiment work reinforces the first-hand/second-hand distinction, and vice versa, within the same Data strand. There is no evidence of dependency or sequence — neither skill is needed to succeed at the other, and the shared token/trigram overlap ('explain', 'the', 'and') is generic — and same-rank developmental direction is not substantively supported, so relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, identical rank 1) sharing the decimal-fraction Content Standard B5.1.4.1. B5.1.4.1.5 asks learners to use models to explain multiplying a decimal (to thousandths) by a whole number, while B5.1.4.1.3 asks them to round decimals to the nearest tenth and hundredth. Both rest on decimal place-value understanding and are mutually reinforcing (rounding supports estimating/checking decimal products; computing products yields decimals worth rounding), but neither statement's proficiency is evidenced as supporting success in the other: rounding is a place-value naming/approximation skill, not a component of modelling decimal multiplication, and no coordinate gap or sequencing evidence supports a developmental direction. Nomination signals (shared parent, same grade, code prefix, adjacent pages, token/trigram overlap on generic strings such as 'the', 'to', 'decimal') are proximity, not dependency. Parent-hierarchy value is limited because both endpoints and the shared parent carry unresolved-ancestry/framework-root fallback warnings, which are not used as positive placement evidence here; the conceptual coherence rests on the statement texts themselves.
